messages:
Maya (AE): FYI ACME POC hit a hard blocker on streaming from their corp network — local tests fine, customer sees repeated TLS handshake failures and 'socket hang up' after ~10s. Can we triage?

Sam (Customer Eng): seeing this in our labs and on a couple of enterprise test VMs behind their corp FW/proxy. Logs: 
```
Error: socket hang up
    at connResetException (internal/errors.js:631:14)
    at Socket.socketCloseListener (_http_client.js:475:22)
    at Socket.emit (events.js:403:35)
    at TCP._handle.close (net.js:677:12)
```
We also see repeated TLS alerts from the proxy: "unexpected_message".

Priya (SE): thanks Sam. Quick Qs: which SDKs are you using (TS/py)? are they streaming over HTTP/2 or chunked HTTP/1.1? also do you have an outbound proxy env like HTTP_PROXY set?

Sam (Customer Eng): they tried both our TS SDK (node 18) and a Python test harness (requests + httpx). Both exhibit the problem when behind corp appliance. From a laptop outside the appliance: streaming is fine. Inside: fails. HTTP/2 for TS stream, Python client defaulted to h2 via httpx.

Alec (Eng): possible cause: corporate proxy doing TLS MITM or terminating TLS and re-negotiating session which can break session resume / early-data for HTTP/2. Also some appliances don't like long-lived upstream connections and will reset after idle/inspection window. Two quick repros to try: 1) force HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming to see if h2-specific behavior; 2) add keepalive pings and lower initial window.

Devon (Infra): can you paste a minimal failing curl / node example so we can reproduce through a lab proxy? also we should enable SDK DEBUG logs. For node, try: 
```
const https = require('https');
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 4 });
fetch(url, { agent, method: 'POST', headers: { 'Transfer-Encoding': 'chunked' } });
```
And run with `NODE_DEBUG=http2,node` to catch handshake frames.

Sam (Customer Eng): sharing test snippet and a capture of the proxy alert. Also getting 429-ish transient rate-limit comments in the app logs when retries kick in.

Priya (SE): notes/questions for ACME: 
- confirm HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY envs and any corporate PAC.
- are they terminating TLS (enterprise certs)? 
- can they allowlist the host for TCP passthrough to test quickly?

Maya (AE): customer asked about pricing impact if we recommend bypassing proxy for production — they want security signoff.

Alec (Eng): from engineering: recommended short-term lab steps: 
1) Test with HTTP/1.1 chunked (node fetch + agent above). 
2) Try forcing the TLS version to TLS1.2/1.3 and disable session resumption to see if proxy resets stop: `NODE_OPTIONS='--tls-min-v1.2'` or Python: `ssl_context.options |= ssl.OP_NO_TICKET` for debug only. 
3) Reduce keepalive interval and enable occasional small pings (if the client supports).

Devon (Infra): additional checks: 
- Confirm corporate proxy isn't injecting `Connection: close` or sniffing frames.
- Capture a tcpdump / Wireshark. Look at the TLS alert code `unexpected_message` points to middlebox.

Sam (Customer Eng): customer can't easily switch off proxy in prod. They will try allowlist to do a quick verify. Meanwhile I ran node with `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` and saw the same reset, so it's not simple cert rejection.

Priya (SE): good datapoint. If MITM persists, we can offer two product workarounds while they negotiate with security: 
- Dedicated (private) deployment with customer-managed egress (VPC/VPN) so traffic never goes through corp appliance; OR
- Use our SDK with a transport wrapper that does more aggressive TCP keepalive + shortened headers to appease proxy (we can ship a patched example for POC).

Maya (AE): customer wants timeline. How long to get a patched sample?

Alec (Eng): I can drop a TS + Python sample by EOD: patched keepalive agent + fallback to HTTP/1.1 streaming and backoff tuning. It will include explicit retry jitter and a flag to disable session tickets for debug.

Devon (Infra): also add a reproducible test script that runs curl through the corp proxy (using `--proxy` and `--http2`) so their infra team can run it locally and share pcap. Example: 
```
curl -v --http2 --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/stream" --data-binary @chunks.bin
```

Sam (Customer Eng): doing that now. One more thing: their security questionnaire asks if we have an "alternate connectivity" option — can you confirm Dedicated/private is possible and what's the onboarding lead time?

Maya (AE): yes we do. I'll send the Dedicated onboarding doc and pricing baseline to Sam.

Priya (SE): technical follow-ups for the sample: include these flags/config knobs in both SDKs: 
- requestTimeout (ms)
- maxRetries with exponential backoff + jitter
- socket keepAlive interval & probe count
- preferHttp1 (boolean)
- debugDisableSessionTickets (debug-only)

Sam (Customer Eng): thanks — I'll forward samples to the customer's infra/security team and get them to run the curl + pcap. Will update here with results.

poc-bot: auto-note: created POC ticket #POC-4721 and assigned to Priya (SE) and Alec (Eng).

Maya (AE): thanks team. If the lab trace shows `unexpected_message` coming from proxy, we escalate to solutions + sales to propose Dedicated + allowlist as the enterprise-approved path.

Alec (Eng): one final gotcha to call out: some enterprise TLS middleboxes don't like TLS record sizes with HTTP/2 frame coalescing. If pcap shows large TLS records, the workaround is to force smaller write sizes at the client (we'll add that toggle to the sample).

Sam (Customer Eng): got it — running tests now, expect initial feedback within 24h.

Priya (SE): will prepare the patched examples and a short note that customers must not use `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` in production — only for ephemeral debugging.

Maya (AE): moving to action items: 
- Sam: run curl + pcap and confirm proxy alert
- Alec/Priya: sample code + debug flags by EOD
- Maya: send Dedicated onboarding + pricing
- Devon: be ready for pcap analysis

Sam (Customer Eng): ack, thanks all.
